subject: Urgent: Skyline Health - Dedicated pool queue ceiling and exec readout
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@skylinehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike: latency, errors and token queueing hitting SLA

Marcus —

We started seeing sustained token queueing and elevated 5xx rates from your dedicated pool around 07:40 PDT this morning. Latency has climbed from our SLA baseline of 120ms p50 to ~950ms p50 and a small percentage of calls are returning errors (rate ~0.9%). This is impacting our triage workflows and delaying patient-facing notifications.

Details:
- First observed: 2025-10-03 07:38 PDT
- Impact: ~10% of requests queued > 2s; overall p50 ~950ms; p95 intermittently >4s
- Recent change: none on our side (no deploys)

We need an urgent ops readout and an understanding of whether reserved throughput is being starved by other noisy tenants or an internal routing issue. Can Redwood provide: current headroom for our dedicated pool, any cross-tenant spillover, and immediate mitigations (routing to hosted fallback, burst authorization, crediting)?

I've attached a short CSV with sample request traces and our SLA for reference. Our CTO David Park is copied for visibility.

Thanks — we need to stabilize within the hour if possible.

— Elena
Elena Soto
Director, Platform Reliability | Skyline Health
Attachments: skyline_trace_sample.csv, skyline_sla_2025.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: latency, errors and token queueing hitting SLA

Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the traces. I'm pulling the dedicated pool metrics now. Short answer: we see a rapid queue depth increase coincident with your window and a small burst from a neighboring workload that exceeded allocation by ~22% for ~6 minutes.

Immediate actions we are taking (now):
- We are enabling cross-region fallback routing for Skyline to offload short, latency-sensitive routes to warm hosted capacity (5–10% of traffic) to reduce tail latency.
- Ops is throttling the noisy neighbor and re-balancing GPU assignments on the pool (estimated 10–15 minutes to finish).
- We will push a soft prioritization policy for your token streams to reduce head-of-line blocking for 60 minutes.

Can you confirm which routes are highest priority (API route names or example IDs)? I'll schedule a 30-min stabilization call with our exec ops and your CTO at 09:00 PDT unless you prefer sooner.

I'll follow up with queue snapshots and a short executive readout.

— Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
Attachments: —

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Skyline Health — immediate ops checklist (internal)

Team — quick playbook:
1) Confirm reservation enforcement: audit token allocation for SK-LINE (DL-5843) and snapshot current QPS vs. reserved throughput. Attach queue dump to ticket.
2) Apply short-term prioritization on route "skyl-notify-v1" and "skyl-triage-predict".
3) Throttle neighbor workload (tenant-id 0x1f3) to bring it within baseline.
4) Enable hosted fallback for 10% of traffic and monitor tail latencies.
5) Authorize 2h burst credits if headroom doesn't reclaim within 15 minutes (I will sign).

I'll be on the stabilization call at 09:00 PDT. Hannah/Soojin: assign the queue snapshot and run the mitigation playbook (mitigation_runbook_v2.pdf). Irene: prepare a short executive slide (2 slides) showing root cause hypothesis + short/med term fixes.

— Marcus

Subject: Re: Spike: latency, errors and token queueing hitting SLA

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the rapid response.

Priority routes: skyl-notify-v1 (patient alerts) and skyl-triage-predict (clinical triage). Those two routes account for ~68% of our P50/P95 sensitivity.

Two asks from our side before the 09:00 stabilization call:
1) Confirmation that the noisy neighbor has been throttled (eventual proof: pre/post queue depth for that tenant).
2) Whether Redwood can authorize a short burst and a one-time credit for the minutes we missed SLA — our procurement team will need a note to justify to finance.

David (cc) is expecting a brief exec readout — if you can include a high-level timeline + what we will do to prevent recurrence that will be perfect.

— Elena

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@skylinehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: latency, errors and token queueing hitting SLA

Elena — quick update after running the mitigation:
- Noisy neighbor throttled at 08:28 PDT; their CPU/GPU share dropped by 30% and we see queue depth for your pool falling steadily. Attached: queue_snapshot_20251003.csv (before/after).
- Hosted fallback routing is live for skyl-notify-v1 (10% traffic) and we see p50 drop toward baseline within two minutes of the change.
- We've provisionally authorized a 2-hour burst allocation for DL-5843; billing will record as a burst credit request. Marcus will confirm final approval for crediting.

For the exec readout (Irene preparing 2 slides):
- Timeline: detection 07:38 → mitigation started 08:25 → throttling applied 08:28 → hosted fallback 08:33 → p50 stabilization 08:36.
- Root cause hypothesis: transient overcommit by neighbor workload + insufficient headroom in the dedicated pool for the current peak pattern.
- Short-term fixes: prioritized routing + soft throttles + burst allocation.
- Medium-term: stronger tenant isolation thresholds, automatic noisy-neighbor detection alert, and suggested reserved capacity increase for Skyline's peak windows.

Elena — will that cover what David needs? If yes, we'll capture credits in a ticket and schedule a postmortem with you for next week.

— Hannah
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: queue_snapshot_20251003.csv

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@skylinehealth.com>, David Park <dpark@skylinehealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Oct 2025 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Skyline stabilization readout + next steps

Hi Elena / David — thanks again for your patience. Short executive summary attached: skyline_sla_2025.pdf and mitigation_runbook_v2.pdf.

What happened (tl;dr): a neighboring tenant exceeded their scheduled burst window and consumed ~22% of the GPU allocation for a 6-minute window, causing queue depth to spike and head-of-line blocking for Skyline's latency-sensitive routes. We applied the following: noisy-neighbor throttle, hosted fallback for selected routes, and a temporary 2-hour burst allocation.

Timeline (high-level):
- 07:38 PDT — Skyline reported degraded p50/p95
- 08:25 PDT — Redwood ops initiated mitigation (throttle + routing)
- 08:33 PDT — Hosted fallback live, queue depth trending down
- 08:36 PDT — p50 returned to ~150ms; p95 still elevated for ~30m while caches warmed

Customer ask: financial credit for the SLA miss. I'm authorizing a one-time credit consideration and have opened a billing ticket to process a credit request for the impacted window. Hannah will follow up with the exact credit amount and the postmortem will include recommendations to remove recurrence risk (tenant isolation, reservation sizing during peak windows).

Next steps:
1) Postmortem (joint) scheduled: 2025-10-10 10:00 PDT — agenda: RCA, mitigation timeline, proposals for reservation adjustments.
2) Short-term: consider a modest reserved-capacity uplift for Skyline during their daily 07:00–09:00 peak.
3) Medium-term: infra team will build an automated noisy-neighbor detector (JIRA-REPL-7123).

If you want the exec readout as a short 10-min call, I'm available at 13:00 PDT today.

— Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
Attachments: skyline_sla_2025.pdf, mitigation_runbook_v2.pdf
